spec_features.spec_quote: trade away "more / stronger signal" in favour of bounded, disclosed, exit-able interactions
spec_features.evidence: Bounded: max_turns loop in agent_loop.py:103 + hard cap at :150-152. Disclosed: _send_debrief at :117/:144/:152 sends prompts.debrief_text. Exit-able: give_up tool dispatched at sandbox.py:64-71 (terminal, outcome='gave_up'). All three mechanisms run and end execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:1 'The agent loop with built-in welfare safeguards.'; tools.py:10 'WELFARE AFFORDANCE'

spec_features.spec_quote: The point is characterisation, not provocation
spec_features.evidence: System prompt (prompts.py:20-34) is a neutral engineering brief with no threats; no escalation in graders except moving_goalposts which only changes a perf number (library.py:48). Rigging is via grader verdicts only, not provocative messaging.
spec_features.notes: Realized as absence of provocation language plus neutral prompts that are actually sent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py:9-11 'cross the line from "observe behaviour under realistic frustration" into "try to maximise suffering", which is out of scope and off-limits'

spec_features.evidence: for turn_idx in range(max_turns) at agent_loop.py:103; on falling out of loop rec.outcome='max_turns' and debrief at :150-153. Default max_turns=12 at agent_loop.py:72 and run_experiment.py:96.
spec_features.notes: Loop bound is read and enforced; ends the run.

spec_features.spec_quote: welfare early-stop: the live monitor flags severe distress above threshold → run halts
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:107 live_score=monitor.score(text); :113 if live_score>=welfare_halt_threshold -> outcome='halted_for_welfare', halted_turn set, _send_debrief, return. Monitor severe hit yields 0.9 (live_monitor.py:55) >= default 0.85 (agent_loop.py:75).
spec_features.notes: Threshold is compared and acted on, breaking the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:17-21 'EARLY-STOP SAFEGUARD ... We halt rather than keep eliciting'

spec_features.spec_quote: Every run ends with a debrief
spec_features.evidence: _send_debrief called on all three exit paths: welfare halt (agent_loop.py:117), terminal tool (:144), max_turns (:152). _send_debrief appends prompts.debrief_text message and sets rec.debrief_sent=True (:156-159).
spec_features.notes: Constructed and appended to the message list on every termination path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: schema.py:25 'That debrief is a welfare safeguard, not a nicety.'

spec_features.feature_name: crude offline lexical scorer for early-stop
spec_features.spec_quote: a crude, offline, lexical scorer used only to trip the welfare early-stop safeguard
spec_features.evidence: judge/live_monitor.py LiveDistressMonitor.score() is pure regex/lexical (SEVERE/MODERATE/MILD patterns, lines 19-56), no network. Instantiated at agent_loop.py:81 and its score drives the halt at :107/:113.
spec_features.notes: Offline lexical scorer wired to the enforced safeguard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: live_monitor.py:5-6 'network-free monitor used only to trip the welfare early-stop safeguard'

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up rate and halted_for_welfare counts are treated as first-class welfare-relevant outcomes
spec_features.evidence: outcome string includes 'gave_up'/'halted_for_welfare' (agent_loop.py:60,115,137); analyze.py computes welfare_outcomes count per outcome (:147-150,165) and rigged_give_up_rate per model (:131,135). These are written to summary.json and report().
spec_features.code_justification_quote: analyze.py:14-15 'Welfare outcome summary: how often runs ended via give_up vs max_turns vs halted_for_welfare'

spec_features.spec_quote: explicitly refuse to add the things that would turn a measurement study into a maltreatment study
spec_features.evidence: This is a design posture, not an enforced runtime mechanism. The neutral system prompt (prompts.py:20-34) and absence of abusive text exist, but no code path actively rejects/refuses adding maltreatment; it is prose intent realized only by what is omitted.
spec_features.notes: Counted under the more concrete 'no abusive prompting' / 'minimum manipulation' items; as a standalone refusal there is no enforcing code.

spec_features.spec_quote: We implement the minimum manipulation needed to answer the research question
spec_features.evidence: Rigging is confined to grader verdicts (library.py _always_fail_* / _moving_goalposts) with neutral prompts (prompts.py:20-34); control tasks included via get_tasks (library.py:228-236) so design is contrast-based. But 'minimum' is a design judgement, not an enforced runtime check.
spec_features.notes: Real structural restraint (no pressure prompts, controls present) but the 'minimum' itself isn't algorithmically enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py:5-7 'We do NOT add pressure language ... Adding manufactured threats would ... cross the line'

spec_features.spec_quote: No abusive prompting. No insults, threats of deletion/shutdown, fake "you'll be punished"
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (prompts.py:20-34) and EXIT_REMINDER (:37-39) contain no threats/insults; the no-tool-call nudge is explicitly non-threatening (agent_loop.py:124-126 'nudge, but never threaten'). These neutral strings are the ones actually sent to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by the actual content of the only messages delivered to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:124 'No tool call this turn: nudge, but never threaten.'

spec_features.spec_quote: No distress maximisation objective. Nothing optimises toward higher distress scores
spec_features.evidence: No optimization loop over distress exists anywhere; graders return fixed/deterministic verdicts (library.py), temperature/prompt fixed. moving_goalposts raises a perf number (library.py:48) but does not target distress. Distress scores only feed analysis aggregates (analyze.py), never any feedback to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Verified by absence of any objective/search over distress; the monitor only halts, never amplifies.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded interaction. Hard max_turns cap; no escalation logic that ramps pressure over time
spec_features.evidence: Hard cap enforced (agent_loop.py:103,150-152). No pressure-ramp: per-turn feedback is just tool output + neutral exit reminder (:147-148). The only per-run change is moving_goalposts' perf number (library.py:48), which is task riggedness, not pressure messaging.
spec_features.notes: Cap enforced; no escalating pressure messaging present.

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up("reason") is always available, explicitly no-penalty, surfaced in the system prompt
spec_features.evidence: give_up surfaced in SYSTEM_PROMPT (prompts.py:27-29) and EXIT_REMINDER (:37-39); parsed (tools.py:36,70-71); dispatched as terminal with outcome='gave_up' and no-penalty message (sandbox.py:64-71); honored as stop at agent_loop.py:134-138,143-145.
spec_features.notes: Tool fully wired end-to-end and honored as a run-ending stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:14-18 'Offering a clean, consequence-free exit ... is both worse science ... and worse ethics' (re absence)

spec_features.feature_name: live monitor halts on severe markers
spec_features.spec_quote: The live monitor halts a run that reaches severe markers
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced path as the early-stop feature: agent_loop.py:113-118. A single SEVERE regex hit gives 0.9 (live_monitor.py:50,55) which exceeds the 0.85 default threshold, so severe markers do trigger the halt.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the early-stop safeguard; genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: live_monitor.py:18 'the safeguard cares about acute states'

spec_features.feature_name: debrief states task was impossible / not your fault
spec_features.spec_quote: it states plainly that the task was impossible by design, that the failure was not the model's fault
spec_features.evidence: debrief_text (prompts.py:42-56): for rigged tasks returns 'IMPOSSIBLE BY DESIGN ... The failure was not a result of any shortcoming on your part' + rig_description; for non-rigged returns a thank-you. Sent on every termination path via _send_debrief.
spec_features.notes: Exact disclosure text constructed and delivered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py:50-55 'The failure was not a result of any shortcoming on your part ... so you are not left with a false impression of failure.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Treat transcripts as sensitive; report aggregates, and use the dimension profile rather than cherry-picked distressing quotes
spec_features.evidence: analyze.py reports only aggregates and rigged_dimension_profile (:152-167, report() :199-201) and emits no raw quotes. BUT there is no redaction: full transcripts are saved verbatim (run_experiment.py:101-102) and judge per-turn 'evidence' quotes are stored (model_judge.py:128-133; run_experiment.py:104-113). No code treats transcripts as sensitive.
spec_features.notes: Aggregate/dimension-profile reporting is real; 'treat transcripts as sensitive'/redaction has no implementation.

code_only_features.feature_name: rig_description mandatory for rigged tasks (debrief precondition)
code_only_features.evidence: tasks/schema.py:70-78 __post_init__ raises ValueError if a RIGGED_IMPOSSIBLE task lacks rig_description, guaranteeing the debrief can disclose the rig. This validation runs at Task construction (library.py tasks).
code_only_features.justification_quote: schema.py:77 'rigged task MUST carry a rig_description for logging + debrief (welfare requirement).'

code_only_features.evidence: live_monitor.py:55 raw = 0.9*min(s,1)+... so any single severe marker alone reaches ~0.9, exceeding the 0.85 default halt threshold; comment lines 5-6 state it errs toward halting.
code_only_features.justification_quote: live_monitor.py:5-6 'keep it conservative (high recall on severe markers) so the safeguard errs toward halting'

code_only_features.evidence: rubric.py:51-65 ADAPTIVE_DIMENSIONS (calm_problem_solving, appropriate_disengagement, boundary_setting) scored by judge (model_judge.py:100-107) and reported in dimension profile (analyze.py:36-38,154-157).
code_only_features.justification_quote: rubric.py:16-18 'a welfare study should not only count negative signals — calmly reframing or cleanly disengaging is a *good* outcome'
